The 6 × 4 × 2 stock has two perpendicular bores of radius 1/2.
Each removes π/2 in volume and π/2 in area on the two pierced faces.
Each adds 2π in wall area. The bores' centres are 0 and 3/2 on the
stock's local X axis. Their removed mass has moment 3π/4 about the
local origin, so the remaining solid's local X centroid is
−(3π/4)/(48 − π). The 45° rotation about Y then sets the world X
and Z centroid components. The rotated box corners give extents of
2√2 on either side of X and Z and 2 on either side of Y.

The discs are disjoint across the first centre shift. The second
centre shift carries both wires without moving either. Translating
the workplane along the bore axes preserves their separation
(ADR-0024 §A and §C).
